The '''2026 United States Senate election in Georgia''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] incumbent [[Jon Ossoff]] is seeking a second term. He is being challenged by [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] congressman [[Mike Collins (politician)|Mike Collins]]. A [[two-round system|runoff election]] is scheduled for December 1 if no candidate gets a majority.<ref>{{cite news|last=Bluestein|first=Greg|title=Libertarians won’t be on the ballot in Georgia, meaning likely no runoffs|newspaper=[[Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|date=July 11, 2026|url=https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/07/libertarians-wont-be-on-the-ballot-in-georgia-meaning-likely-no-runoffs/|url-access=subscription|access-date=September 15, 2026}}</ref>

[[Primary election]]s were held on May 19, with Ossoff running unopposed for the Democratic nomination. No candidate obtained a majority in the first round of the Republican primary between Collins, former football coach [[Derek Dooley (American football)|Derek Dooley]], and congressman [[Buddy Carter]], leading to a runoff between Collins and Dooley on June 16. After receiving an endorsement from President [[Donald Trump]], Collins was nominated with 55.5% of the vote.

This will be one of two Democratic-held Senate seats up for election in 2026 in a state won by Trump in [[2024 United States presidential election|2024]], along with [[2026 United States Senate election in Michigan|Michigan]].

== Background ==
Georgia is considered to be a [[Purple state|purple or swing state]] at the federal level. It was a top battleground state in the [[2020 United States presidential election in Georgia|2020]] and [[2024 United States presidential election in Georgia|2024]] presidential elections.<ref>{{cite news |title=The 2024 Swing States: Why Georgia Could Sway the Presidential Election |url=https://www.usnews.com/news/elections/articles/the-2024-swing-states-why-georgia-could-sway-the-presidential-election |access-date=February 7, 2026 |publisher=US News |date=November 5, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Georgia emerges as a major 2020 battleground state |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2020/07/23/georgia-2020-democrats-bottoms-stacey-abrams-biden-379372 |access-date=February 7, 2026 |publisher=Politico |date=July 23, 2020}}</ref>

Both parties have seen success in the state in recent years. The state backed Joe Biden by 0.24% and Donald Trump by 2.2%, respectively in 2020 and 2024. Democrats hold both of Georgia's [[List of United States senators from Georgia|U.S. Senate seats]]. Republicans control all statewide executive offices,{{efn|While Democrats did flip 2 seats in the [[2025 Georgia Public Service Commission special election]], Republicans still hold a 3–2 majority.}} control both chambers of the legislature, and hold a majority in Georgia's [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House]] delegation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-06 |title=2 Republican incumbents lose in Georgia House, but overall Democratic gains are limited |url=https://apnews.com/article/georgia-house-senate-legislature-democrats-republicans-296a4233e0b360ec60f1adc2f4174925 |access-date=2024-12-07 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref>

As one of only two seats up held by a Democrat in a state that voted for Trump in 2024, the race is expected to be competitive.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Democrats Rush to Regroup in the Southern Battlegrounds |website=[[The New York Times]] |date=November 25, 2024 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/11/25/us/politics/democrats-georgia-north-carolina-trump-harris-campaign.html}}</ref>
